sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- CENTCOM's own account] CENTCOM said US forces carried out 'self-defense' strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island after Iran 'launched several ballistic missiles towards regional neighbours' and that the missiles 'all failed to hit their intended targets'. CENTCOM: 'Two Iranian missiles fired at Kuwait fell short or broke apart en route, and three missiles launched at Bahrain were immediately intercepted by US and Bahrain air defense forces.' Air raid sirens were heard in both Bahrain and Kuwait. CENTCOM also said US forces 'successfully defeated multiple Iranian ballistic missiles and drones'. The Qeshm strikes hit Iranian radar / drone-control / air-defence sites at Goruk and Qeshm Island. [CONTEXT, already recorded] Trump confirmed the limited Qeshm strikes Friday (0700-01); IRNA reported a US MQ-1 drone downed over Qeshm (16th of its kind); CENTCOM described the situation as 'relatively calm'. sections.what_verified: 1 distinct declared-tier publisher family, and that family IS the primary source itself: CENTCOM / US DoD (T1, STATE US, OFFICIAL-PD) -- its own X post, quoted verbatim with the same figures (2 Kuwait fell short, 3 Bahrain intercepted) across UNB, Dubai92, watchdogreport, usnewsnetwork and daily360. Those carriers are UNDECLARED in the registry -- attribution only, never counted. primary_source_single_family: true.
sections.what_disputed: IRGC claims (via aggregators straightnews/daily360, undeclared) that its missiles/drones hit US sites in Kuwait and Bahrain, claiming 8 (elsewhere 21) US sites destroyed including the US Fifth Fleet HQ and Ali Al Salem Air Base. CENTCOM says those claims are false: no US casualties, no base damage. Bahrain reported damage to a residential building near the airport, not at Fifth Fleet HQ. No independent battle-damage assessment has been published.
sections.why_matters: Iran fired ballistic missiles at two US allies in one night -- and CENTCOM says every single one failed. Two fell out of the sky over Kuwait. Three were shot down over Bahrain. Then the US hit Qeshm.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP -- CENTCOM: Iran fired ballistic missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain Friday night; 2 at Kuwait fell short, 3 at Bahrain intercepted; Qeshm strikes were the self-defence response

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran fired ballistic missiles at two US allies in one night -- and CENTCOM says every single one failed. Two fell out of the sky over Kuwait. Three were shot down over Bahrain. Then the US hit Qeshm. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Did Iran actually hit anything -- or did every missile fail? CENTCOM says zero got through; the IRGC claims eight US sites destroyed. Whose count do you believe?
